sub_strands.sub_strand: Polite Language (Theme 1: Citizenship)
learning_experiences: define the term euphemism,
identify examples of polite words and expressions used in a poem or story,
listen to an audio interview and identify euphemism,
simulate an interview from a text and identify euphemism,
use euphemism in a conversation,
make rules for a debating session in groups,
conduct a debate in small groups on titles such as ‘passengers can avert road crashes’,
watch or listen to a recorded clip of a debating session in parliament,
create posters with euphemistic words and phrases,
share the posters through social media or the school notice board.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we use polite language?
Why is it embarrassing to say some words in public?
How can we show good citizenship with regards to road safety?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner speaks engangingly and listens critically to compare perspectives when participating in debates.
Citizenship: It is nurtured as the learner engages in constructive dialogue when practising the use of polite language.
sub_strands.values: Respect: It is inculcated as the learner displays patience with others when adhering to debating conventions and using polite language.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: It is enhanced as the learner practises the use of euphemism in various contexts.
sub_strands.links: The learner is able to relate the concept of polite words and expressions to their learning of living with others in Religious Education.

outcomes.text: outline words and phrases used to express euphemism

skills.name: Use euphemisms to show politeness
skills.mastery: The child replaces blunt words with polite ones where tact is needed (passed away for died, senior citizen for old person, washroom for toilet, between jobs for jobless) and knows what each means. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

sub_strands.sub_strand: Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text (Theme 1: Citizenship)
learning_experiences: identify reading materials in a variety of subjects,
search for online fiction and non-fiction texts,
skim through a text to obtain the gist (main idea),
scan a text on 'safe road infrastructure' to obtain specific details,
read the text,

maintain a reading log showing their reading activities and thoughts about what they read. The items to include in the log are: - the title and author of the text, - the dates you read, - the amount of time you spend reading each day, - the key themes in the text, - the major characters, - the plot development, - the questions you have as you read,
engage in follow up activities such as: - creating chain stories, - forming a book club, - keeping vocabulary journals, - preparing a reading log for the titles of the fiction and non-fiction texts.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to read different types of materials?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to learn: It takes place as the learner builds on their own learning experience when selecting reading materials.
Critical thinking and problem solving: It is promoted as the learner follows simple instruction to develop a good reading culture.
Self-efficacy: It is nurtured as the learner shows concerted attention when creating a reading log.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: It is inculcated as the learner engages in assigned roles when searching for reading materials, reads, and keeps a reading log.
Integrity: It is enhanced as the learner displays transparency in using the internet when searching for online fiction and non-fiction texts.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: It is developed as the learner shares reading materials and experiences.
sub_strands.links: The learner is able to relate the concept of intensive and extensive reading to their learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili

identify the parts of an email in their peer's work by underlining the elements,
learners to rework their emails to include any elements that were missing,
display some of the emails on the talking walls.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we write emails?
What is the difference between emails and letters?

rubrics.heading: Suggested Assessment Rubric: Listening and Speaking

indicators.indicator: Ability to use polite language during conversations and use verbal and non-verbal cues during negotiations.

levels.EE: uses polite language during conversations and easily uses verbal and non- verbal cues during negotiations.
levels.ME: The learner always uses polite language during conversations uses verbal and non-verbal cues during negotiations.
levels.AE: The learner uses polite language during most conversations and uses verbal and non- verbal cues during negotiations. The learner listens
levels.BE: The learner uses polite language during some conversations and rarely uses verbal and non- verbal cues during negotiations.

indicators.indicator: Ability to listen to oral poetry and use oral performance techniques appropriately.

levels.EE: The learner listens to oral poetry and uses varied oral performance techniques appropriately.
levels.ME: The learner listens to oral poetry and uses most oral narrative performance techniques appropriately.
levels.AE: to oral poetry and uses some oral narrative performance techniques appropriately.
levels.BE: The learner listens to oral poetry but uses few oral narrative performance techniques approprately.

indicators.indicator: Ability to deliver speeches, oral reports and express appropriate feelings towards subject matter of poems.

levels.EE: The learner fluently delivers speeches, oral reports and effortlessly expresses appropriate feelings towards subject matter of poems .
levels.ME: The learner fluently delivers speeches, oral reports and expresses appropriate feelings towards subject matter of poems.
levels.AE: The learner delivers speeches, oral reports and with some inconsistencies expresses appropriate
levels.BE: The learner delivers speeches, oral reports with many inconsistencies and rarely expresses

indicators.indicator: Ability to listen for main idea, general idea, specific details and information from texts and take notes.

levels.EE: The learner listens for main idea, general idea, specific details and information from texts and take notes with ease and precision.
levels.ME: The learner listens for main idea, general idea, specific details and information from texts and take notes with ease.
levels.AE: The learner listens for main idea, general idea, specific details and information from texts and take notes with some inconsistencies.
levels.BE: The learner listens for main idea, general idea, specific details and information from texts and take notes with many inconsistencies.

indicators.indicator: Ability to articulate given sounds, and apply stress and intonation appropriately in given texts.

levels.EE: The learner articulates all the target consonant and vowel sounds correctly and applies stress and intonation with ease.
levels.ME: The learner articulates most the target consonant and vowel sounds correctly and uses stress and intonation.
levels.AE: The learner articulates some of the target consonant and vowel sounds correctly and applies stress and intonation in some contexts.
levels.BE: The learner articulates a few of the target consonant and vowel sounds correctly and finds it difficulty to apply stress and intonation.

indicators.indicator: Ability to distinguish between reading for meaning, information and infer meanings of words and phrases and use contextual clues.

levels.EE: The learner effortlessly distinguishes between reading for meaning, information and infers meanings of all the words and phrases and use contextual clues with ease.
levels.ME: The learner distinguishes between reading for meaning, information and infers meanings of all words and phrases and uses most contextual clues.
levels.AE: The learner partially distinguishes between reading for meaning, information and infer meanings of some words and phrases and uses some contextual clues.
levels.BE: The learner rarely distinguishes between reading for meaning, information and infer meanings of few words and phrases and struggles to use some contextual clues.

indicators.indicator: Ability to read a text, interpret it, make notes and summarise information.

levels.EE: The learner reads and correctly interprets a text, makes notes with precision and summarises information with ease.
levels.ME: The learner reads and correctly interprets a text, makes notes and summarises information with ease.
levels.AE: The learner reads and struggles to interpret a text, makes some notes and summarises information with help.
levels.BE: The learner reads and is unable to interpret a text, barely makes notes and does not summarise information even with help.

indicators.indicator: Ability to make connection between texts and real life, summarise events and answer direct and inferential questions from poems.

levels.EE: The learner effortlessly makes all connections between texts and real life and provides examples, summarises events and answers all direct and inferential questions from poems.
levels.ME: The learner makes most connections between texts and real life, summarises events and answers all direct and inferential questions from poems.
levels.AE: The learner makes some connections between texts and real life, summarises events and answers some direct and inferential questions from poems.
levels.BE: The learner makes few connections between texts and real life, struggles to summarise events and answers few direct and inferential questions from poems.

indicators.indicator: Ability to create mental images from texts. features of short forms of oral literature, explain their functions and perform them appropriately.

levels.EE: The learner creates a variety of mental images from texts with ease. The learner identifies all features of short forms of oral literature, concisely explains their functions and creatively performs them with ease.
levels.ME: The learner creates mental images from texts with ease. The learner identifies all features of short forms of oral literature, explains their functions and performs them with ease.
levels.AE: The learner creates mental images from texts. The learner identifies most features of short forms of oral literature, explains some their functions and performs them with some difficulty.
levels.BE: The learner creates mental images from texts. The learner identifies some features of short forms of oral literature, explains some their functions and performs them with a lot of difficulties.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify simple props and costumes that create the mood and present a dramatized part of a play to the audience.

levels.EE: The learner easily identifies simple props and costumes that create mood, and creatively presents a dramatized part of a play to the audience.
levels.ME: The learner identifies simple props and costumes that create mood, and presents a dramatized part of a play to the audience.
levels.AE: simple props and costumes with assistance, and attempts to dramatize part of a play to the audience but with some difficulty.
levels.BE: The learner is unable to identify simple props and costumes and has difficulty dramatizing part of the play to the audience.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify and read fictional and non- fictional texts for independent reading and information.

levels.EE: The learner excellently identifies and reads a variety of non- fictional texts independent reading and records experiences from the reading sessions for tracking progress.
levels.ME: The learner identifies and reads a variety of fictional and non-fictional texts for independent reading and information.
levels.AE: The learner identifies some texts for independent reading with assistance.
levels.BE: The learner makes an attempt to identify some texts for independent reading even with assistance.

indicators.indicator: Ability to keep a portfolio of the fiction materials they have read.

levels.EE: The learner keeps a detailed portfolio of a variety of texts.
levels.ME: The learner keeps a portfolio of a variety of texts.
levels.AE: The learner keeps a simple portfolio of a few texts.
levels.BE: The learner keeps a scanty portfolio of one text.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify main points, make notes and writes a summary.

levels.EE: The learner accurately identifies all the main points, makes notes and writes a summary with ease.
levels.ME: The learner identifies all the main points, makes notes and writes a summary.
levels.AE: The learner identifies some main points, makes notes and writes a summary in exhaustively.
levels.BE: The learner identifies few main points, make shoddy notes and write a sketchy summary.

indicators.indicator: Ability to skim, scan and apply fluency strategies while reading.

levels.EE: The learner aptly and easily skims and scans a text and applies all fluency strategies while reading.
levels.ME: The learner applies skimming and scanning with ease and applies all fluency strategies while reading.
levels.AE: The learner applies skimming and scanning with some struggles and some fluency strategies while reading.
levels.BE: The learner struggles to skim and scan and applies few fluency strategies while reading.

indicators.indicator: Ability to use different parts of speech in sentences.

levels.EE: The learner uses all the different parts of speech accurately and in a variety of sentences.
levels.ME: The learner uses all the different parts of speech and in sentences.
levels.AE: The learner uses most parts of speech and in sentences.
levels.BE: The learner uses few parts of speech and in sentences.

indicators.indicator: Ability to construct different types of sentences.

levels.EE: The learner creatively constructs all the different types of sentences with ease.
levels.ME: The learner creatively all the constructs different types of sentences.
levels.AE: The learner constructs most of the different types of sentences.
levels.BE: The learner constructs some types of sentences with assistance.

indicators.indicator: Ability to use gender neutral language, correct order of adjectives, numerals and ordinals in sentences.

levels.EE: The learner always uses gender neutral language, correct order of adjectives, numerals and ordinals with ease in sentences.
levels.ME: The learner always uses gender neutral language, correct order of adjectives, numerals and ordinals in sentences.
levels.AE: The learner most of the times uses gender neutral language, correct order of adjectives, numerals and ordinals in sentences.
levels.BE: The learner rarely uses gender neutral language, correct order of adjectives, numerals and ordinals in sentences.

indicators.indicator: Ability to write a well-developed paragraph.

levels.EE: The learner writes a well- developed Paragraph effortlessly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner writes a well- developed Paragraph consistently.
levels.AE: The learner writes a paragraph but leaves out some details.
levels.BE: The learner writes a paragraph but it lacks most details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to write different documents using correct format. composition using correct punctuation, handwriting and specified idioms.

levels.EE: The learner writes different documents using correct format with ease and uses correct tone and vocabulary. The learner writes a composition in neat and legible handwriting, correctly spells words, punctuates it and creatively uses specified idioms with ease.
levels.ME: The learner writes different documents using correct format with ease. The learner writes a composition in neat and legible handwriting, correctly spells words, punctuates it and creatively uses specified idioms.
levels.AE: The learner writes some documents using correct format but struggles with tone and vocabulary. The learner writes a composition in neat and legible handwriting, has some spelling errors, struggles to punctuate it, and uses some specified idioms.
levels.BE: The learner barely writes any documents using correct format, and vocabulary. The learner writes a composition illegible handwriting, has little command of punctuation is unable to use specified idioms.

indicators.indicator: Ability to apply the writing process in writing and assess a composition using predestined criteria.

levels.EE: The learner aptly and meticulously applies the writing process and accurately assesses a composition using predestined criteria.
levels.ME: The learner applies the writing process and accurately assesses a composition using predestined criteria.
levels.AE: The learner applies the writing process with assistance and struggles to assess a composition but leaves out some aspects of the predestined criteria.
levels.BE: The learner barely applies the writing process and assesses composition leaving out many aspects of the predestined criteria.
